title: Pool ops midweek prep and followup
content:
Goal: use the 30–45m sync to (1) align on reservation asks for next quarter, (2) validate autoscale knobs for the top 3 noisy tenants, and (3) capture concrete follow-ups for finance/sales/infra.

Background quick hits:
- Current committed pool: 96 A100s across two pools (east/us and eu-west).
- Avg weekday utilization (last 14 days): 68% peak hours, 42% off-peak.
- 7-day p95 latency regressions observed when runqueue > 220k tokens/s (see CAP-3421).
- Burst policy currently allowed up to +20% for 3 hours/day per org.

Agenda (30m):
1) 5m — TL;DR numbers and runway scenarios (opt/likely/pessimistic)
2) 10m — Reservation proposals (sizes, gating, contract length) + quick revenue-impact rationale
3) 8m — Autoscale policy tweaks for noisy tenants + KV/prefix caching opportunities
4) 5m — Open blockers / ask list for Sales/Finance/Infra + assign action owners

Runway scenarios (back-of-envelope):
- Optimistic: 10% net efficiency gain from caching + model swaps => postpone +8 GPUs for next quarter
- Likely: status quo => need +12 GPUs to keep p95 SLOs at current traffic growth (~6% w/w)
- Pessimistic: two mid-sized customers increase sustained usage => need +26 GPUs or enable immediate burst-policy extension

Questions I want answered in the meeting:
- Sales: which committed deals target next-quarter activation windows? (names + expected ramp week)
- Finance: how flexible is commit start date? can we backdate consumption credits to cover slow ramp?
- Infra: what is the current lead time for adding GPUs to eu pool? any rack/PSU constraints?

Autoscale knobs to propose (short list):
- Reduce minimum instance count for low-priority pools from 8 -> 4 during 00:00–08:00 local to save warm GPU-hours
- Add a throughput-based trigger that scales out at runqueue > 150k tokens/s (instead of wait for token latency)
- Implement a temporary weighted-fair-share for top 3 tenants causing >60% tail variance

Follow-ups (explicit owners + due):
- Diego: prepare 2 slides showing per-tenant token-hour breakdown + 14d trend (due 2026-03-12)
- Priya: draft reservation options (3, 6, 12 month) with pricing/discount deltas and break-even calc (due 2026-03-13)
- Ethan: run quick sim to estimate cache hit uplift if we enable prefix caching for GenAI workloads (due 2026-03-14)
- Me (Anjali): open CAP ticket to adjust autoscale trigger and capture expected savings; add test plan (due 2026-03-11)
- Sales: (ask during sync) get list of customers likely to commit this quarter + tentative start dates (capture by 2026-03-15)

Notes to self (scratch):
- Bring the sample SLO chart that overlays queue depth vs p95 latency — visuals sell the ask.
- Keep pricing convo anchored to $/GPU-hour and show cost delta with caching scenario.
- If infra lead time > 4 weeks, push for a burst-commit hybrid option with Finance.

Risks / unknowns:
- New multi-tenant job type from customer X that spikes KV lookups (could blow memory pressure) — need triage if appears after commit
- EU procurement cycle for one large account may delay payments and affect starting date

Quick wins to mention if asked:
- Enable pre-warm windows aligned to known daily ramp (we already have 2-hour pre-warm window; tweak to 3 hours only for 2 tenants)
- Short-term holdback: cap non-committed orgs to 75% of max burst capacity during market open hours

Meeting deliverable (end state):
- Reservation ask (count + term) agreed by Ops + Sales + Finance OR a fallback plan with burst-extension and autoscale changes.
- Owners assigned for every action with dates.

Voice: this is a personal prep doc — keep it informal in the meeting but convert follow-ups to JIRA afterwards.

Last-minute checklist before the sync:
- [ ] Pull latest 14d utilization table (metrics-read only)
- [ ] Export p95 latency vs queue depth plot
- [ ] Create 1-slide reservation ask summary (numbers + rationale)
- [ ] Prep 2 quick examples of noisy tenant runs to cite in policy change section

End.
